name: Aqua Blue
lede: Aqua Blue is a vivid, bright cyan, a screen-era color named for the look of water.

sections.title: The name
sections.body:
Paterson defines aqua blue as a light greenish blue [1]. The same dictionary notes that Aqua, on its own, was adopted by web page creators as a color name [1]. The swatch here comes from the xkcd color survey, and the library also files it under ISCC-NBS block 171 [2].

It is more saturated than the dictionary's "light" suggests. The library's nearest standard name is [[aqua]], at a distance of 10.2, which is a clearly visible gap [2]. It sits in the blue-green stretch of the wheel, between [[blue]] and [[green]], close to [[turquoise]] [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our archive of 23,781 has this color covering at least 1% of its canvas, as photographed [3]. That describes our archive, not painting as a whole [3]. It is a color of screens and signs more than of oil paint, and the books we hold say nothing more about it [1][3].

notes.cite: Paterson, A Dictionary of Colour, p. 31, "aqua blue"
